title: "Come Who Will," the Voice from Heaven
description: "Come Who Will," the Voice from Heaven in Tonic Solfa to OMNI DIE, doh is F: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 3 verses and a piano.
about: These words were printed without an author's name in A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion, compiled by Samuel Longfellow and Samuel Johnson (Boston, 1848), as hymn 159, “Invitation”.

The book printed the words without tunes, marked Eights and Sevens (8.7.8.7) (8.7.8.7), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to OMNI DIE; any other Eights and Sevens (8.7.8.7) tune fits them as well.
underlay: "Come who will," the voice from hea-ven, Like a sil-ver trum-pet, calls; "Come who will," the church hath giv-en Back the e-cho from its walls.

lines: "Come who will," the voice from heaven,
"Come who will," — the church hath given
Back the echo from its walls.
Come, where God, his gifts bestowing,
In the church on earth is known.
While his eye with rapture glistens,

source: A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1848)
licence: Public domain: anonymous words in print by 1848.
credits: Words anonymous, public domain, as printed in A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1848); set to OMNI DIE by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
